name: Claypot fish
summary: Cá kho tộ is the claypot fish in the Châu Đốc food chapter. Vietnam Tourism calls it a Mekong Delta dish, cooked for hours until the fish flakes, and eaten with rice and greens. It is not a town-only recipe. No stall price was published.
origin: A Mekong Delta dish in the Châu Đốc chapter, not a recipe that belongs only to this town.
culture: The charms chapter places the pot with the other Châu Đốc dishes, and it labels the cooking as delta food. You order it when you want a main meal in town, not as a market breakfast. Bún cá is the morning bowl. This is the pot.
texture: Vietnam Tourism says the fish is cooked for hours in a clay pot until it flakes. Eat it with hot rice and greens. A finer texture note was not on the page.
howToEat: Order it as a main meal and eat it with hot rice and greens, the way the charms chapter tells you to.

Bún cá, with điên điển, chili, and lime, is the market morning. Lẩu mắm is the dinner on the place page. The charms chapter’s other shared dinner is a seafood hotpot of vegetables, mushrooms, noodles, and herbs.
Town kitchens cook the claypot. A shop was not named. A stall price was not printed. Check on arrival.
where: Town kitchens in Châu Đốc. The charms chapter does not name a shop for the claypot. It names a hotel terrace on the river.
